#+title: Nix and backend descriptions as Source data

* Describe a backend

A =.bl= backend description contains one data value. For example:

#+begin_src clojure
{:version 1
 :kind :local
 :nix {"settings" {"max-jobs" 1 "cores" 4
                    "extra-system-features" ["kvm"]
                    "extra-sandbox-paths" ["/dev/kvm"]}}}
#+end_src

=:kind= selects =:local=, =:configured=, =:ssh= or =:nixbuild=. The =:nix= map
uses Nix's =settings=, =buildMachines= and =distributedBuilds= options directly.
Remote descriptions set =max-jobs= to zero and declare their builders. The
[[../../tooling/build-backends][repository descriptions]] show each kind. Credentials belong to host
configuration or CI secrets; descriptions contain credential locations.

Compile descriptions with the repository-owned codec:

#+begin_src sh
./bin/bl run scripts/compile-build-backends.bl -- tooling/build-backends/*.bl
./bin/bl run scripts/compile-build-backends.bl -- --check tooling/build-backends/*.bl
#+end_src

=build.backend/compile= reads data without evaluating Source, validates the
description, emits Nix and checks the inverse through =build.backend/from-nix=.
The adjacent =.nix= file records the exact Source digest. Bootstrap clients
verify that digest before applying configuration. The SDK qualification checks
the full compilation again, including exact generated bytes.

This projection lets a clean client select its backend before producing an SDK.
Backend selection needs Nix evaluation of a small data expression; it starts no
BEAM and depends on no previous compiler installation.

* Use the same description on a host and in CI

For NixOS, import the generated policy through the module factory:

#+begin_src nix
imports = [ (beam-lisp.lib.build-backend ./build-backend.bl) ];
#+end_src

The module checks the Source digest and applies the description's Nix options.
An optional =:evaluation= map with string keys =storeUri= and =transport= emits
the finite station endpoint description. Ordinary Nix remote builds need only
the builder configuration.

CI selects a description path with =CI_BUILD_DESCRIPTION=. Set it to
=tooling/build-backends/nixbuild.bl= to use nixbuild.net, and supply the
=NIXBUILD_TOKEN= secret. The worker action reads the generated Nix projection,
sets up provider authentication and applies the compiled client options.
Backend kinds and capacity are declared in Source. Runner labels remain CI
orchestration configuration.

* Read, generate and edit Nix

=nix= is a first-party namespace backed by =native/bl_nix=:

#+begin_src clojure
(ns example (:require [nix :as nix]))
(def document (nix/read "{ count = 2; # keep this comment\n}"))
(nix/data document)                 ;; => {"count" 2}
(nix/text (nix/set document ["count"] 3))
(nix/emit {"count" 3})
#+end_src

The codec preserves every byte when reading and printing an existing document.
Emission and projection preserve plain data. Lambdas, recursive bindings and
other computed expressions are refused by the data projection; callers can
retain them explicitly as =:nix/expr= syntax through ={:unsupported :tag}=.
The backend compiler accepts plain configuration data only. Nix itself performs
evaluation and realization.
